uiWithFullPrivilegeLinuxProgramsRunWithA:
With privileged Shell, Linux programs run with Android's elevated permissions (the shell access that USB debugging grants). Apps and tools that need deeper access to the device, which cannot run with ordinary app permissions, become possible.

At the same time, if a malicious program gets into the container (a package, a script, an AppImage, a game…), it could use those permissions to cause security problems on your device, such as:
• installing or removing apps without asking
• capturing the screen, or tapping and typing for you
• reading other apps' logs and files in your storage
• changing system settings
• reading passwords stored in the Linux keyring, or being watched by other privileged apps

Install software only from sources you trust. To try software of unknown origin, run Linux as Android (ordinary app permissions) instead.
